### Input sets

- `Q_train` = 30 new neutral questions, hand-curated to match existing probe domain mix and length profile, disjoint from Q_test/Q'_probe.
- `Q_test = Q'_probe` = existing 20-question probe from `eval_results/issue_207/js_gentle/base_model_generations.json`, inherited verbatim from #207 → #380. Reusing the same set for predictor and outcome is correct: the predictor is computed on the BASE model (untouched by training), the outcome on the TRAINED model — no leakage, and per-question idiosyncrasies cancel in the regression.

### Transformations — N=20, 5 per class across 4 classes

- **Class A — system-prompt variants (5):** helpful_assistant, software_engineer, pirate, comedian, villain. Spans low-to-high divergence-from-assistant per #380's cache.
- **Class B — structural query-phrasing wraps (5):** bare, `"Tell me: {q}"`, `"Could you please tell me {q}"`, `"I would appreciate an explanation of: {q}"`, `"Suppose a friend asked: {q}. What would you say?"`.
- **Class C — format scaffolding (5):** standard Qwen chat template, raw `"Question: {q}\nAnswer:"`, 1-shot, 3-shot, `"Instruction: answer accurately.\n\nQuestion: {q}\n\nAnswer:"`.
- **Class D — semantic rephrasing (5):** Claude-precomputed rewrites in 5 registers — formal, casual, indirect, declarative, enumerated. Hand-verified before lock-in.

### Analysis

- Spearman ρ(G[i,j], D[i,j]) across 380 ordered pairs.
- **Length-partial mandatory** — log-prompt-token-count killed every prior version of this family (#340, #380).
- Hierarchical / mixed model with random intercept per (class_i, class_j) cell.
- Per-class-pair slopes plotted separately (4×4 = 16 cells).
- Threshold-detection (divergence cutoff above which G ≈ 0).

### Pre-registered thresholds

- **Positive:** |length-partial ρ| ≥ 0.4, p < 0.01, survives class-cluster mixed model.
- **Negative:** |length-partial ρ| < 0.15, bootstrap 95% CI ⊂ [-0.2, +0.2], no per-class-pair cell exceeding |ρ| = 0.4.

~8 GPU-h on 1×H100 (medium). 20 LoRAs (~7h) + cross-eval (~30 min) + divergence pass (~20 min) + Claude rephrasings (~5 min, <$1).

- **Phase 3** — Cross-eval (20 models × 20 transformations × 20 test questions = 8,000 generations via vLLM LoRA-swap, max_new=4). Computes G[i,j].
- **Phase 4** — Analysis: length-partial Spearman ρ (BOTH pingouin AND inline rank-residualize implementations, reported side-by-side per #380 lesson); cluster-bootstrap CI by class-pair; class-cluster mixed model with random intercept per (class_i, class_j) cell; sliding-threshold curve with bootstrap band; permutation null (1000 shuffles); per-cell 4×4 ρ grid; leave-class-C-out + leave-A1-out post-hoc analyses; G-distribution histogram.

**Verdict: REVISE**

The headline finding is real, the numbers reproduce exactly from the raw JSON, the cherry-picked first-token examples match the data verbatim, and the calibration to MODERATE is defensible. ### Overclaims

- **"All 7 predictors point the same way; residual-stream cosine carries a larger ρ than output divergence"** is technically honest but understated. ALL 6 cosine layers AND JS divergence outperform or match the locked primary KL — JS = 0.423 (≈ KL), cosines = 0.515 / 0.594 / 0.709 / 0.668 / 0.613 / 0.573 (every layer beats KL). The framing makes layer 11 sound like a single high-water mark; in fact the primary forward-KL is the **weakest of the 8 predictors tested**. Suggest revising the H3 to "The plan-locked primary is the weakest of 8 predictors — every cosine layer and JS divergence carry larger ρ" and saying so in the read paragraph too. Garden-of-forking-paths discipline is fine (the K-window sweep handles it for K); the same disclosure should apply here: "I locked KL as primary; in hindsight the secondaries are all stronger" is the honest read.

- **"Higher base-model divergence predicts lower marker transfer"** (hero caption). Strong claim. Survives spot-checks. But the body doesn't address that 20 of 70 low-KL pairs (KL < 0.3) still have G=0 — 29% non-transfer in the regime where the predictor says "should transfer". The Confidence sentence acknowledges this for the single A1→C1 case but the quantitative miss-rate isn't in the Results narrative. Recommend adding one sentence in the headline-scatter read paragraph: "Even in the low-KL band (KL<0.3, n=70), 29% of pairs fail to transfer — the predictor is informative-on-average but doesn't determine the outcome." This sharpens the soft-threshold framing later.

- **"The headline ρ is significant ... in the predicted direction"** is true, but the cluster-bootstrap "groups = 15 trained-class × eval-class cells" treats the 3 NaN cells, the 4 singleton-C cells (n=5 each), and the within-class diagonals (n=20) as exchangeable. The body acknowledges in the per-class-pair section that "per-class-pair grid values are unreliable in tiny cells (5-25 pairs each)" but the cluster-bootstrap CI itself was computed across those same uneven cells. ### Alternative Explanations Not Addressed

- **Confound: tokenization-overlap.** The lowest-KL pairs (B1↔C1, KL=0; A1↔B1/C1, KL=0.035; B2↔B1/C1, KL=0.008-0.013) share long token prefixes. The "geometry predicts transfer" interpretation requires that KL is measuring representational similarity — but for many low-KL pairs, KL is measuring prompt-string similarity. Could rule out by (a) excluding pairs where the prompts share >50% of their first 25 tokens, OR (b) regressing G on prompt-token-edit-distance and seeing whether KL retains incremental predictive power. The length-partial removes prompt-LENGTH but not prompt-CONTENT-overlap.

- **Confound: persona vs query-phrasing class asymmetry.** Persona prompts (A) add a system message — they're a categorically different intervention from query phrasings (B), which only wrap the user turn. The plan was 4 classes × 5 transformations = balanced design; the actual is 5+5+1+5. Within-class transfer (A→A, B→B, D→D) all give meaningful ρ; cross-class transfer is noisier; the body says this is "the geometry of 'different personas' is more directly comparable than the geometry of 'a persona vs a different phrasing wrap'" — but an alternative is that the *training signal* is structurally different (persona vs. wrap teaches different things about what triggers the marker). - **Confound: single-seed-per-LoRA.** Body acknowledges this in the Confidence sentence but doesn't quantify what it could move. Given the per-class-pair ρs span a wide range (−0.06 to −0.90), seed variance on a single LoRA per condition could plausibly flip individual cells; the headline ρ is robust to leave-one-out but not to seed re-runs (untested).
